newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-GRAF ADVANCES, ANXIOUS WAIT IN STORE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-GRAF ADVANCES, ANXIOUS WAIT IN STORE.

text.p: Steffi Graf overcame Romania's Irina Spirlea on a windy Sunday afternoon at Roland Garros, but a couple of restless days await the German who must now plan a strategy to beat her bete noire, South African Amanda Coetzer.
Second seed Graf trailed by a set at the French Open for the first time since 1993, before taming 13th seed Spirlea 6-7 6-2 6-2.

The five-times champion, who will appear in the quarter-finals for the 12th consecutive year, received a warning from the 11th-seeded Coetzer who will aim to beat her for the third time this year when the pair meet on Tuesday.
"I'm very excited," said Coetzer, who advanced to the last eight by beating Spain's Conchita Martinez for the first time on Sunday.

"I have a lot of firsts here, beating Conchita and reaching the quarter-finals for the first time," added the diminutive South African. "Steffi has obviously been injured and hasn't been able to play as much as she wanted to. There's an opportunity for me."

Graf, still wearing a bandage on the injured left knee which sidelined her for three months earlier in the season, started tentatively and wasted a set point before losing the first set in a tie-break.

"I didn't start off too well," she said. "In the beginning of the first set, she (Spirlea) played very well, serving well, going for her shots and being aggressive. But from the middle of the first set, I started to play better."

The wind, which sent clouds of red dust swirling around centre court, made life difficult for both players but Graf kept her cool, showing glimpses of her best form to take control of the match in the next two sets.

"It was good to play a match under difficult conditions and to fight it out," said Graf, ousted from top spot in the world rankings by Swiss teenager Martina Hingis in March. "I'm slowly finding my rhythm, I haven't been feeling that well for weeks."

Graf now has to prepare for Coetzer, who has beaten her in two of their three meetings this season, including an embarrassing 6-0 6-1 victory at the German Open and a straight sets fourth round win at the Australian Open.
"I'm looking forward to it," said Graf. "She's very consistent, she uses the court well and she's quick on her feet. The main thing against her is patience."
Coetzer said she was ready for a marathon: "All I know is that I can stay out there as long as I have to and that's all I'm concerned with," she said.
